headline: Umno is collecting Najib's RM50m fine into a party account. No law limits or names the donors.
context: On 18 September 2026 the Pardons Board made Najib Razak's house arrest conditional on paying a RM50 million fine set in 2024. Umno launched a fund the same day. Malaysia has no political-financing law. A government committee recommended one in 2016; the minister now says 2027.

cards.big: Najib's RM50 million fine became a condition of house arrest on 18 September. By evening Umno was collecting for it in a party account: RM634,562 in three hours, by its own count.
cards.sub: No law caps a gift to a party or names the giver in public. The Bar calls the gap a lacuna; the minister says 2027.

cards.big: Tabung Solidariti Najib Razak takes gifts into an account in Umno's registered name, supervised by party HQ. Its launch set no cap, donor rule or audit.
cards.sub: Accounts go to the Registrar of Societies; under section 10(2) only members may obtain them. A fine is not campaign money; the gap is the same.

cards.big: Najib announced the committee that first recommended the Act on 14 August 2015, amid the furore over RM2.6 billion in his accounts. The minister now says 2027.
cards.sub: It reported in 2016. Buku Harapan pledged the Act in 2018. GIACC said 'next month' in 2019. Cabinet agreed in principle to draft it in 2023.

cards.big: On 8 September the minister drafting the Act said, as a lawyer: without it 'many politicians will be charged with corruption'.
cards.sub: Azalina Othman Said is also Umno information chief. A 2026 index put PKR, DAP, Amanah, Bersatu and PAS all under 30% on financial accountability; none names donors.

cards.big: A fine can be crowdfunded through a party account only members may see. That is not a loophole in the political-financing law. There is no such law.
It is like a bank that promised a know-your-customer rule in 2015, studied it under four governments, and still takes deposits with no form to fill.
cards.sub: The 2016 committee wrote the form: gifts above RM3,000 reported within 30 days, foreign cash banned, government contractors barred, no cap on amounts.

cards.big: The fine is raised in an account only party members may see, under a law that does not exist. Pakatan Harapan promised it in 2018; its government says 2027. One is a choice.

revisions: CORRECTED (Stage 3): headline 'Umno opened an account to pay Najib's RM50m fine' → 'Umno is collecting Najib's RM50m fine into a party account'. Umno Online (S9) supplies an account in the party's registered name; it does not say a new or dedicated account was opened.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): headline/hook sub 'No law says who may give a party money, how much, or whether the public may know' → 'No law limits or names the donors' / 'no law that caps a gift to a party or names the giver in public'. Narrowed to the two things a dedicated statute would add (caps, public disclosure); existing Societies Act filing duties are acknowledged on the Legal card.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): Legal sub 'section 29 gives copies to members and subscribers, not the public' → 'under section 10(2) only members may obtain them'. Section 29 sits in Part II (mutual benefit societies only); s.10(2) is the operative bar. Official reprint re-read this session.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): reframe/view 'nobody outside the party may inspect' → 'only members may see'. The Registrar holds the accounts and has inspection powers (ss.14, 27); the bar is on non-members obtaining them from the Registrar.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): Governance big 'the committee that first drafted the law' → 'the committee that first recommended the Act'. NCCPF produced 32 recommendations for a proposed Political Donations and Expenditure Act; it did not draft a bill.

Stage 3 reports a Jan 2026 Hansard describing the 2023 step as a referral of the policy scope to a select committee; both are official, the card uses the narrower 'agreed in principle to draft'.

introduced_claims.claim: WFD/UKM 2026 index: PKR 29.17, DAP 29.17, Amanah 25.00, Bersatu 17.39, PAS 20.83 on financial accountability; 'No party publicly reveals donor identities'. Umno not assessed.
BHEUU: no specific law currently regulates political funds; study began under GIACC in 2019; BHEUU took over May 2023; Cabinet agreed in principle 8 Sep 2023.
The fund's stated purpose is to help pay the fine; the account is in Umno's registered name and supervised by Umno HQ.

synthesis_notes: Over-integration calls. (1) Stage 2 wants the Pardons Board's process scrutinised; Stage 5 agrees the pardon is out of scope but wants the 'political use of the condition' named. The evidence supports neither as a card: Article 42 is a prerogative and the board's reasons are not published; the cards keep the pardon as the dated fact that created the condition. Declined both. (2) Stage 2 flags a category error (criminal fine vs campaign finance); Stage 5 calls the lawful-fund framing cowardice. Stage 2 is right on the distinction and the Legal sub now states it; Stage 5 is right that legality is not the finding, and the reframe already says so. Not averaged: both points are made, in their own places. (3) Stage 5's hard truths on Malay piety, Islamic branding of the fund, Zahid's discontinued charges and MCA history are declined: 3R exposure and anger-at-person, and none changes the mechanism. Its verified cross-party index is accepted because it makes the issue less partisan, not more. (4) Stage 3's 8 Sep 2023 reading (referral to select committee) vs BHEUU's own page (agreed in principle to drafting): both official; the card uses BHEUU's wording, which is the narrower claim about drafting and matches the minister's speech; the brief logs the discrepancy. Compression: May 2022 (JKKMAR) dropped from the Governance sub for length and because Stage 3 showed it was a committee, not Cabinet; the '90.3% before GE16' figure dropped because BHEUU's published pages do not carry it; the '1,544' figure dropped with it. Naming consistency: 'the Act' for the missing statute, 'the fund' / 'Tabung Solidariti Najib Razak' for the drive, 'the fine' throughout. Elevated word: 'lacuna' (hook sub), the Bar's own term. Reframe family: hard sentence ('There is no such law.'); the last two published reframes (2011 causal, 2012 unknown) do not share it. Emotion check: hook reads anger-at-process (a condition set, a collection opened, no rule); no card reads as sadness.
